judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Brisk airship-captain drop-off with a concrete objective and spells handed over; 'Good luck and good speed' and 'This may get very ugly, lad' have Westwood's plain, slightly stagey ring.

items.label: B
items.critique: Exclamatory fanfare with double dashes and a three-step goal list compressed into one line; the one-line reminder 'You need to press on now, lad' is typical Westwood minimalism.

items.label: C
items.critique: Clipped fragments ('You'll know. And careful.') and a reminder that repeats the opening almost verbatim, a Westwood habit; journal phrased flatly.

items.label: D
items.critique: Short, functional, with the idiosyncratic 'No more time for chit-chat' reminder and the melodramatic 'You remain our only hope'; reads like shipped Nox.

items.label: E
items.critique: Smoothly crafted with motivated details (why the ship can't fly closer, why the potions); 'Mind how you go' and 'Down the road with you' feel like a modern writer doing a gruff captain.

items.label: F
items.critique: Long, expository speech that explains backstory step by step ('My attempts to send for help have come to nothing'); the agreement slip is plausible either side, but the length and tidy causality read new.

items.label: G
items.critique: Sentences pack several clauses and plot links ('I'm certain [Person] is behind the Urchin raids too'); more connective tissue than Westwood's terse briefings.

items.label: H
items.critique: Overloaded exclamation ('What kept you, lad!?') and run-on causal chain about trade and hunger; stakes are spelled out economically in a way Nox rarely bothers with.

items.label: I
items.critique: Stiff, slightly odd phrasing ('The Master for the [Place]', 'convey the [Thing]') and capitalised 'YOU' are authentic Westwood quirks; reads as a real, unpolished campaign line.

items.label: J
items.critique: Competent but list-like set-up (go here, find him, take potions and gold, visit the forge, take the road) that reads as a designer's checklist turned into speech; reminder is generic.

tells: Westwood's openings are terse and functional, often with fragments and one-line reminders; the new texts explain motivation and backstory (why the ship stops here, why the road matters, who stole what) in longer, well-joined sentences.
New texts chain cause and consequence across several clauses ('with the gate shut, no cart can get down... leaving... the least of our troubles'); Westwood rarely builds stakes so logically.

Westwood lines carry small oddities of phrasing and emphasis (capitalised YOU, 'The Master for the', a reminder that repeats the opening); the new texts are cleaner and more idiomatically 'gruff', using stock folksy phrases ('Mind how you go', 'Down the road with you').
New texts bundle several errands into one briefing (find a person, collect items, visit a shop, take a road); Westwood's opening gives one clear objective.
Recurring generic set pieces across the new texts (an old watchtower held by raiders, a closed north road, Ogre raids on farms) suggest a shared template rather than distinct chapters.
